objectives.OBJ-01: Define a Glean Agent and identify who agents are for.
objectives.OBJ-02: Name the five core building blocks that every agent combines.
objectives.OBJ-03: Choose Auto mode, Workflow mode, or an independent agent for a stated need.
objectives.OBJ-04: Match the right trigger to how people will start the agent.
objectives.OBJ-05: Apply least privilege, permission behavior, and risk-matched process.

items.stem: A partner asks you to define a Glean Agent in one sentence. Which answer is accurate?

options.text: A reusable AI solution that uses instructions, knowledge, tools, and context to complete tasks.
A saved search that reruns automatically and emails the results.
A chatbot that answers questions from a single uploaded knowledge base.
A connector that indexes a new data source so it becomes searchable.

items.stem: Which of these are among the five core building blocks that every agent combines? Select all that apply.

options.text: Goal and instructions
Knowledge and context
Output and memory
Billing and cost centre
Index refresh schedule

items.stem: A customer needs an agent that runs the same five steps in the same order every time, because an auditor will review the output. Which mode fits?

options.text: Workflow mode, because it gives explicit control over each step, branch, and hand-off.
Auto mode, because the agent will work out the best path each time.
Either one, because both produce identical execution paths.
Neither — auditable work cannot be done with an agent.

items.stem: An agent must start automatically whenever a document changes in a connected tool, and act on what changed. Which trigger, and how does the agent receive the change?

options.text: A content trigger, and the changed content is passed in as [[Trigger input]].
A chat message trigger, and the user pastes the change into the chatbox.
An input form trigger, and the user selects the document from a multiple choice field.
A schedule trigger, and the agent re-reads the whole source each run.

items.stem: A partner publishes an HR agent to a Slack channel as visible to everyone in the channel, and reports that it returns less than the same agent in the web app. What is happening?

options.text: Expected behavior: for channel-wide visibility the agent only uses documents accessible to all channel members, which prevents restricted content being exposed in a broad channel.
A defect — permissions should be identical on every surface, so it should be escalated as a bug.
The agent lost its permissions when published, and the owner must re-grant document access.
Slack does not support knowledge retrieval, so the agent falls back to web search.

items.stem: Your partner is scoping an agent that will be company-wide, read restricted data, and update Jira tickets. What does the lifecycle guidance say about process?

options.text: Apply a comprehensive process: rigorous testing, formal review, and launch planning.
Apply a lightweight process, then add review only if users complain.
Process depth is a matter of team preference and is not tied to scope.
Skip the lifecycle, because write tools are blocked by the platform anyway.
